skill.name: ops-inspector
skill.description: Guides read-only CloudBase health checks across environments, logs, cloud functions, CloudRun services, and databases.
skill.summary: Inspect CloudBase resource health and error patterns with a read-only AIOps workflow.
skill.author: tencentcloudbase

security_audit.summary: The static external command, network, and filesystem findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, URLs, and sibling skill references. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. A medium semantic risk remains because the log inspection workflow lacks explicit redaction guidance for sensitive log data.

remediation.issue: Sensitive data may appear in function logs or CLS search results.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required redaction step before reporting log excerpts, including masking credentials, tokens, personal data, and internal identifiers.

remediation.issue: Operational inspection can expose resource inventory and incident details.
remediation.suggestion: State that the workflow must run only for authorized users in an authenticated, bound CloudBase environment.

content.value_statement: CloudBase teams need a fast way to understand resource health, logs, and service status during incidents. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through read-only inspections and prioritized recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the active CloudBase environment is accessible.
Verifies CLS log service status before log-based diagnosis.
Lists cloud functions and reviews recent function errors.
Inspects CloudRun service status, details, and common failure signals.
Searches CLS logs for error patterns across tcb and tcbr services.
Produces a severity-based inspection report with console links.
limitations: It diagnoses issues but does not deploy resources or change code.
It requires authenticated CloudBase MCP tools and a bound environment.
Log analysis is limited when CLS is disabled or time ranges are missing.
It provides point-in-time inspection, not continuous monitoring.

use_cases.title: Run Incident Triage
use_cases.description: Check CloudBase service states, recent errors, and likely failure areas during an incident.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Function Failures
use_cases.description: Review cloud function status and recent logs before deciding which implementation skill to use.

use_cases.title: Review Environment Health
use_cases.description: Prepare a point-in-time health summary for CloudBase resources and log service coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Health Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my bound CloudBase environment. Check environment access, CLS status, cloud functions, CloudRun services, and recent error patterns. Summarize severity and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Target a Function Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose the cloud function named <functionName>. Review recent function logs and related CLS errors for the last 24 hours. List likely causes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Service Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect CloudRun services and cloud functions for the last <timeRange>. Correlate errors across services and identify shared failure windows.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Incident Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a targeted inspection for the incident at <timeWindow>. Include affected resources, log patterns, root cause hypotheses, remediation priorities, and console links.

output_examples.input: Run a full CloudBase health check for the bound environment.
output: Overall health shows warnings. CLS is enabled, and most services are reachable.
One cloud function has repeated timeout errors in the last 24 hours.
Recommended next step is to inspect database latency and the function timeout setting.

output_examples.input: Diagnose errors for the payment cloud function.
output: The function is deployed, but recent logs show repeated memory pressure.
The likely cause is oversized request processing or a dependency loading issue.
Increase memory only after reviewing recent code changes and payload size.

output_examples.input: Check CloudRun service api-prod after a 502 incident.
output: The service is running, but error logs cluster around the reported time window.
Health check failures and upstream timeouts appear together.
Review readiness checks, container startup time, and downstream database availability.

best_practices: Confirm environment access and user authorization before querying resources.
Set a clear time range before searching logs.
Redact secrets and personal data before sharing log excerpts.
anti_patterns: Run broad log searches without a time window.
Treat one error line as the root cause without correlation.
Use the skill to deploy fixes instead of diagnosis.

faq.question: Does this skill change CloudBase resources?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only diagnosis and recommendations.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects authenticated CloudBase MCP tools for environment, log, function, CloudRun, and database inspection.

faq.question: Can it inspect logs when CLS is disabled?
faq.answer: No. It first checks CLS status and reports a warning when log search is unavailable.

faq.question: Can it find the exact root cause every time?
faq.answer: No. It forms likely causes from resource status, logs, and error patterns.

faq.question: When should another skill be used?
faq.answer: Use an implementation skill after this inspection identifies code, CloudRun, database, or platform changes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for incident reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It produces severity summaries, error patterns, recommendations, and relevant console links.
